title: Surge compensation & capacity costing: volume trigger model (Q3 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a compact set of surge scenarios tying customer volume triggers to short-term compensation and capacity levers. Goal is to provide a quick decision protocol for growth-inflected token demand spikes (30–300% above baseline) so Finance + Eng can respond within 7–14 days without breaking unit economics for the quarter.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We model three surge bands (minor, moderate, major) and two response levers: (A) temporary contractor capacity / overtime (fast, high unit cost) and (B) stepped hiring + reserved GPU commitments (slower, lower unit cost). Pricing sensitivity is tested by +/-10% and +/-25% price moves to check revenue coverage vs incremental cost. Early recommendation: for 30–80% short spikes use contractor/overtime + soft throttles; for multi-week >100% increases, accelerate hire pipeline and buy short-duration reserved capacity to avoid long tail GPU egress costs.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline monthly token volume (Q2 run-rate): 120B tokens served (combined embedding + generation).
- Average token price realized (net of discounts): $0.0008 per token (blended).
- Baseline gross margin on hosted API: 45% before S&M and G&A; cost per 1M tokens served baseline = $800.
- GPU marginal cost (on-demand avg): $12k per GPU-month; reserved short-term (1–3 months) negotiated at ~20% discount when committing 8+ GPUs.
- Contractor backend engineer fully loaded rate: $25k/month (effective capacity: 0.6 FTE-equivalent for burst infra tasks).
- Ramp times: contractors 3–7 days; fulltime hires 8–12 weeks (sourcing + notice).
- Elasticity: assumed short-run demand elasticity to a price raise is -0.25 (conservative); to a price cut is +0.4.

Scenario definitions and response matrix:
- Minor surge (30% above baseline for <=14 days): use contractor + temporary 2–4 GPU on-demand burst. Apply soft rate-limiting on low-priority customers.
- Moderate surge (50–120% above baseline for 2–6 weeks): mix contractors + short reserved capacity (4–16 GPUs, 1–3 months), initiate expedited hiring (1–2 roles).
- Major surge (>120% sustained >6 weeks): open hiring for 3–6 roles (infra/ops), reserve 16+ GPUs with tiered commitments and consider short-term price adjustments for new signups.

Compact cost table (monthly equivalents, illustrative):

Scenario | Delta tokens (M) | Extra GPUs (mo) | Contractor FTE-mo | Incremental cost est ($k/mo) | Recommended immediate lever
Minor   | 36,000           | 2               | 0.6               | 62                          | Contractors + on-demand GPUs
Moderate| 60,000           | 8               | 1.8               | 320                         | Mixed contractors + short reserves
Major   | 150,000          | 24              | 5.0               | 1,200                       | Hire + reserved commitments

Notes on the table: delta tokens are millions; incremental cost includes GPU amortization, extra egress, contractor fees, and incidental infra. These are working numbers for planning cadence, not final quotes.

Pricing sensitivity checks (high level):
- Base price: $0.0008/token. For each scenario, run P&L under price variations of -25%, -10%, +10%, +25%.
- Example (Moderate surge): additional revenue at base = 60,000M * $0.0008 = $48M; incremental cost estimate = $320k/mo (note: discrepancy arises because revenue scale is monthly tokens vs cost buckets — in practice revenue scales by customer composition and commit discounts; this sheet uses blended proxies for decisioning).
- Quick rule: if a price increase of +10% reduces expected churn by <5% (elasticity <0.5) and covers incremental GPU/resourcing cost, prefer price tilt for new enterprise signups while grandfathering existing committed customers.

Headcount playbook (burst-focused roles):
- Short list of priority hires for multi-week surges: (1) Infra SRE (burst capacity lead), (2) Serving runtime engineer (ops automation), (3) Capacity planner (finance/ops combo), (4) Partner sales engineer (enterprise onboarding).
- Hiring phasing: triage hires (1–2 contractors converted to FT if surge persists 8+ weeks).
- Cost per FT hire (fully loaded): avg comp $210k + taxes/benefits ~35% = ~283k/year -> ~23.6k/month.

Decision triggers (operational):
- Trigger A (Day 0–7): sustained 20% week-over-week increase for 3 days -> escalate to on-call infra + open contractor requisition.
- Trigger B (Day 8–21): sustained >50% WoW for 7 days -> finance to authorize short reserved GPU block (4–16 GPUs) + fast-track 1 hire.
- Trigger C (>21 days): >100% vs baseline for 14+ days -> open multi-role hiring pipeline and negotiate 1–3 month reserved capacity at scale.

Runway & budget impacts (short note):
- Operate under a contingency bucket (quarterly) sized at 4% of Opex to cover surge contractors and short reserve purchases; for Redwood scale today that is ~ $1.2–1.6M per quarter (buffer arithmetic: baseline Opex ~ $40M/Q * 4%).
- If a major surge materializes and we accelerate hiring, we recommend use of the contingency bucket + reallocation from discretionary S&M for Q3 only; longer-term we fold sustained costs into the regular FY budgeting cycle.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- We need a tighter mapping from customer cohort (enterprise vs self-serve) to margin contribution during surges. Current blended revenue numbers hide concentration risk.
- Can SRE/infra build a fast-turn kernel that reduces per-token marginal GPU cost in the first 14 days? If yes, contractor -> capital tradeoff changes.
- Legal: any price change cadence constraints for committed customers? Tie to product for grandfathering rules.

Action items (owner tags):
- Maya: run the +/-10% pricing sensitivity sweep across top 25 enterprise accounts and provide a churn estimate by 2026-07-09.
- Priya (FinOps): draft a 3-month reserved-capacity offer template for customers to help offset our short-term committed cost by 2026-07-12.
- Diego (SRE): validate 2–4 GPU burst boot time and cold-start cost estimates by 2026-07-05.

Appendix (quick calc snippets):
- Contractor cost logic: 1 contractor @ $25k/mo produces ~0.6 FTE infra output for burst tasks -> effective per-month cost per FTE-eff = $41.7k.
- GPU amortization: 1 GPU-month on-demand $12k; 8 GPU-month reserved short block negotiated $9.6k/GPU-mo -> break-even depends on sustained utilization >70%.

Working doc notes (tone): this is intentionally concise and action-oriented — use it as the 'first-mover' playbook during demand spikes. Longer form modeling with cohort-level revenue curves should live in the cost-models repo linked above.
